answer: Each AI agent in the economy stakes a bond and every hour must solve a challenge derived from its own past outputs and a global random nonce, costing roughly 0.03 GPU-hours per proof. A sybil cannot copy one answer because the challenge branches like a vine from that identity’s private history, and a reused or cloned proof produces no valid echo in the verification network. To plant ten thousand fake agents in the meadow, an attacker must run ten thousand separate accelerators and pay about two megawatt-hours daily, making the attack linear and expensive.
